column1: # THE BYTE-FREEZE REGISTRY.  Data, not prose.  Read by tests/byte-freeze.rs.
# AGENTS.md rule 47: record the WHOLE invocation beside every hash -- the flags
# you left at their default AND the environment you ran it in.  A hash without
# its command is not a weak record, it is not a record at all.  The test does not
# merely *check* the rows against a command written somewhere else -- it BUILDS
# the command and the environment out of the row, so the hash and the invocation
# cannot drift apart, and one milestone's flag can never be spliced onto another
# milestone's command.  That splice is fact 1379: it cost a 1.9-hour
# investigation into a regression that had not happened.
# The environment columns are not theoretical rigour.  An earlier draft of rule
# 47 bound only "directory, --limit and --gate by value" -- all CLI flags -- and
# within two hours a freeze was found that reproduces EXACTLY but only under
# STREHL_ALIGN=0, a value that appeared nowhere in its record.  Three false
# breaks in one session came from this one root cause: `bee-3-cpl` lost --gate,
# `coffee-bean` lost STREHL_ALIGN.
# TAB-separated.  Blank lines and lines beginning with `#` are ignored.  The
# header row is checked verbatim, so renaming or reordering a column fails loudly
# instead of silently shifting every field one to the left.
# COLUMNS
#   id              kebab-case, unique.  Names the invocation, not the milestone.
#   stack           leaf directory under the capture library (see `capture_library`
#                   in byte-freeze.rs; $STREHL_CAPTURES overrides).  A leaf, never
#                   a path: the library root is machine-local and belongs in an
#                   environment variable, not in a frozen record.
#   frames          FIRST..LAST that --limit actually selects, VERIFIED against the
#                   directory before anything is rendered.  "limit 20" is not
#                   reproducible without knowing which twenty: --limit takes a
#                   PREFIX in name order, so one file added to the front of a
#                   bracket reframes every freeze on it and the hash moves for a
#                   reason that has nothing to do with the renderer.
#   limit           --limit, always explicit.
#   gate            --gate, always explicit AND ALWAYS BY VALUE.  `default` is a
#                   rejected value: DEFAULT_GATE moved once already and the
#                   absence of this one flag is the whole of fact 1379.
#   srgb            yes|no -- whether --srgb is passed.
#   -- the environment.  `unset` is a VALUE, spelled out, never an empty field:
#      the defect rule 47 names is that a reader cannot tell a default from an
#      omission.  Every variable in RENDER_ENV is removed before these are
#      applied, so the ambient environment of whoever runs the test cannot
#      quietly render a different pipeline than the row describes.
#   env_align       STREHL_ALIGN.  `0` = registration off.  `unset` = on.
#   env_warpmap     STREHL_WARPMAP.  A fixture file under tests/data, or `unset`.
#                   Setting it makes the row read a COMMITTED warp map and write
#                   nothing anywhere (merge_cmd.rs:1035).
#                   env_align=unset with env_warpmap=unset is a SOLVING row and is
#                   rejected by the parser, with the measurement, on sight.
#   env_fix_halo    STREHL_FIX_HALO, by value or `unset`.  (STREHL_FIX_HALO_DELTA
#                   is only read when this is set, and is cleared with it.)
#   env_cache_dir   STREHL_CACHE_DIR.  Must be `scratch`: the harness supplies an
#                   empty per-run directory.  The real default is a SHARED per-user
#                   cache, and a freeze that reads it is a freeze that depends on
#                   whatever another agent last solved on this machine.
#   alignment_mode  what the tool must REPORT on stderr for this row.  ASSERTED,
#                   before any hash is compared.  This column is the OBSERVATION;
#                   env_align/env_warpmap are the SETTING.  A silent flip of this
#                   field is exactly what M86c did.
#                   `on-sidecar-cache` is a legal observation and an ILLEGAL
#                   record -- see the parser.
#   sha256          uppercase hex, 64 chars.  Never truncated: the corpus already
#                   carries a freeze recorded as `D99F5D82...76CA`, which no
#                   machine can check.
#   bytes           expected file size.
#   workers         the chunking the baseline was measured under.  REPORTED, NOT
#                   ASSERTED -- it is a property of the measuring host (RAM and
#                   core count), and a mismatch here is the first thing to suspect
#                   when a hash moves on a machine that is not the one above.
#   baselined_at    the commit at which this row's hash was last measured.
#   baselined_on    YYYY-MM-DD.
#   why             WHY the hash is what it is, and what moved it last.  This is
#                   the column that would have prevented fact 1379.  It is checked
#                   for length and for placeholders; when you re-baseline a row,
#                   REWRITE IT.  A `why` describing the previous re-baseline is
#                   worse than an empty one, because it reads as current.
# ADDING A ROW: freezing everything is the same as freezing nothing.  See
# docs/research/M108-freeze-test.md section 5 for what earns a row and what
# does not.

column17: RE-BASELINED at 2525e08. Both coffee-bean rows moved together and both are mine. ATTRIBUTION PROVEN BY ISOLATING THE VARIABLE, NOT BY BLAMING A COMMIT RANGE: re-rendering this row's own recorded invocation with the CURRENT binary and STREHL_EDGE_AWARE=0 reproduces the previous baseline BIT-EXACTLY (experiments/BUILD-HALO/attribute_freeze.py). That is strictly stronger than pinning my parent commit, which could only show the bytes differ ACROSS a boundary and could not separate my change from anything else in the same range -- and it incidentally clears every other agent's commits since 9695b3c of touching these bytes. WHAT MOVED THEM: debc8ea 'halo: solve the selection radius from the noise model, and ship it on' made the edge-aware adaptive selection radius the shipped default -- edge_aware_arm() returns EdgeArm::Acuity when STREHL_EDGE_AWARE is unset -- so the focus window now collapses near a depth silhouette instead of standing at WINDOW_RADIUS=13 everywhere. That changes which frame wins at edge pixels, so the merged bytes move. ce2c793 'halo: gate the collapse on proof that collapsing buys something' then moved them AGAIN, requiring BimodalStats::peak_excess to clear the gate before a pixel may cap its radius -- a veto, so it collapses in strictly FEWER places than debc8ea did, not more. NOT A REGRESSION AND NOT A DEFECT IN THE RENDERER: a deliberate change to the render path is exactly what these rows exist to catch, and they caught it. The only defect was that it sat unrecorded and read as unattributed, which is how the next agent to touch this path re-baselines it believing their own change caused it and absorbs someone else's delta into their justification. FIXED WITH THIS BASELINE: STREHL_EDGE_AWARE, STREHL_EDGE_TAU, STREHL_EDGE_CONF and STREHL_ONLY_FRAME are now in RENDER_ENV and cleared before the render. They were not, and every one re-routes the election -- STREHL_ONLY_FRAME renders a single frame with NO election at all -- so until now these hashes silently depended on the ambient environment of whoever ran the test. That is the STREHL_ALIGN=0 defect described in this file's own header, committed a second time by me when I added the variables and not the entries. Both hashes below were measured with all four confirmed unset. bytes are unchanged at 49450019: the geometry did not move, only the pixel VALUES. THIS ROW: registration is OFF, because align_enabled() short-circuits before any cache path is computed, so no shared state can reach it. Superseded value 89958637..C218 was the pre-debc8ea baseline at 9695b3c and is the value the arm-off control reproduces. V-TONE independently measured CC1468A3..523A from a git-archive pin of debc8ea's parent -- a correct measurement of the state AFTER the radius change and BEFORE the veto. Do not paste CC1468A3 in: it is a real hash of a real commit, but not of what ships.

column17: RE-BASELINED at 96571ee, and the move is INTENDED. WHAT MOVED THEM: lateral-CA correction now defaults ON. align_cmd.rs called active_profile(), which reads STREHL_FIX_CA and returns None when unset; unset was the default, so every render the owner has ever seen ran with a measured, tested correction switched off because nothing called it (fact 1449's defect class). It now calls profile_for_capture_env, which applies the profile iff the body model and composed lens id in the FILE match the ones it was measured on, and declines on Unknown. ATTRIBUTION PROVEN BY ISOLATING THE VARIABLE, NOT BY BLAMING A COMMIT RANGE, following the standard BUILD-HALO set on this row at 2525e08: re-rendering this row's OWN recorded invocation from a clean git-archive pin of 96571ee with STREHL_FIX_CA=off reproduces the superseded baseline 6325922C..27D8F BIT-EXACTLY, and with it unset reproduces the value below bit-exactly (experiments/BUILD-RENDER-hotpix/attribute_ca_freeze.py, 4/4). Both arms are required: 'off reproduces the old bytes' alone would also be satisfied by a build that ignored the flag and moved nothing. That incidentally clears every other commit since 2525e08 of touching these bytes, and clears the four uncommitted files other agents had in the shared tree when this was measured. ONLY THE SIDECAR ROW MOVED, AND THAT IS THE LOCALISATION SIGNATURE THIS FILE'S HEADER PREDICTS: the correction is applied during warp application, so the unaligned row -- which applies no warp -- is unchanged at 3162EB0B..781A, exactly the 'if only the sidecar row moves, warp application changed' case. A change that moved both rows would have been a merge-core change and would not have been mine. FIXED WITH THIS BASELINE: STREHL_FIX_CA is now in RENDER_ENV and cleared before the render. It was not, and this is the same unrecorded-input defect the header describes and the EDGE_AWARE comment admits committing a second time -- with a new twist worth recording, because it generalises: the variable is OLD and the omission never bit while unset meant off, since the only reachable ambient state matched the recorded pipeline. Defaulting it ON turned a dormant unrecorded input into a live one WITHOUT ANYTHING IN THIS FILE CHANGING. scripts\gallery.ps1 sets this variable, so 'ran the gallery, then ran the tests, in one shell' is a real path to a mismatched hash, not a hypothetical one. A clear-list is not made safe by being complete on the day it was written. Superseded value 6325922C..27D8F was the pre-default-on baseline at 2525e08 and is the value the STREHL_FIX_CA=off control reproduces. bytes are unchanged at 49450019: the geometry did not move, only the pixel VALUES.
